title: Check yourself: the lifecycle the host starts and the one that goes wrong

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Your client's QMUX has one request listener, which answers 0800 echoes (code 301) and nothing else. Links A and B sit behind a pool with check-enabled, and the sign-on manager signs on once per connection and echoes every five minutes. At 23:40 host A sends an 0800 with code 002, and it goes on answering echoes as usual. What happens to the purchases the pool sends to link A over the following hours?

options.text: The host declines them, since the client still treats the connection as signed on and keeps routing purchases to it
options.says: the 002 ends on the unhandled queue; the logon mark still matches, the echoes are answered, so the link stays enabled until the logon mark expires

options.text: The host declines them until the next echo, since the manager takes the link out when an echo follows a host sign-off
options.says: the host keeps answering echoes, so every echo succeeds and nothing takes the link out

options.text: They all go to link B instead, since QMUX answers the 002 itself and removes the enabled mark of link A
options.says: QMUX answers nothing by itself; a message nobody waits for goes to the listeners and then to the unhandled queue

options.text: They all go to link B instead, since the adaptor drops a connection that the host has signed off and connects again
options.says: a sign-off is a message on the connection; the adaptor neither reads it nor closes the connection

origin.section: 15.1 The Host Starts Network Messages Too, and Each One Needs Its Own Answer

questions.stem: After a refused sign-on, a client waits 5 seconds, doubles the wait after each further refusal, and caps it at 10 minutes. The host refuses every sign-on from 01:00 and accepts them again from 03:00. When does the link carry purchases again?

options.text: At the first sign-on after 03:00, which may come up to 10 minutes later, since the wait stops growing at the cap
options.says: the cap is also the longest a link can stay out after its host has recovered

options.text: At the first sign-on after 03:00, which may come hours later, since the wait keeps doubling while the host refuses
options.says: the doubling stops at the cap, so no wait is longer than 10 minutes

options.text: Within a second or so of 03:00, since the host's change of mind resets the client's wait at once
options.says: the client learns that the host accepts again only from its next sign-on, which comes when its wait is over

options.text: Within a second or so of 03:00, since once the wait reaches the cap the manager tries again on every pass
options.says: at the cap the manager waits the cap between attempts; trying on every pass is what the backoff replaces

origin.section: 15.2 A Refused Sign-On Waits Longer Each Time

questions.stem: Two links share a pool. The manager's echo timeout is 20 seconds, and it takes a link out after 4 failed echoes in a row. Host A's application hangs just as an echo goes out. Purchases arrive at 6 a second, split evenly between the links. What happens to purchases until link A leaves the pool?

options.text: Roughly 240 go to A and get no answer, since A stays in the pool for about four echo timeouts
options.says: each failure the limit allows keeps the dead host in the pool for one more echo timeout: about 80 s at 3 purchases a second

options.text: Roughly 60 go to A and get no answer, since A leaves the pool at the first failed echo and later ones only confirm it
options.says: the link stays enabled until the limit-th failure in a row; the first failure only starts the count

options.text: None of them go to A after the hang, since the pool skips a link as soon as one of its purchases times out
options.says: the pool looks only at the connection and the enabled mark; a purchase timing out changes neither

options.text: None of them go to A after the hang, since QMUX holds back purchases while an echo on the link is unanswered
options.says: QMUX sends every request it is given; an echo waiting for its answer does not stop other requests

origin.section: 15.3 One Lost Echo Is Not a Dead Host

questions.stem: A release stops Q2 at 10:15:00. The sign-on manager's stop takes the link out of the pool, signs it off and forgets the session, without waiting for anything. A purchase sent at 10:14:59.8 is approved by the host at 10:15:01. The caller's timeout is 15 seconds. What does the caller get?

options.text: null at about 10:15:15, so it must reverse the purchase, since the approval found the connection already closed
options.says: Q2 undeploys the QMUX and the adaptor right after the manager's stop; the answer is lost and the outcome is unknown

options.text: null at about 10:15:15, so it may send the purchase again later, since a host that was signed off discards the purchase
options.says: the host received the purchase before the sign-off and approved it; sending it again charges twice

options.text: the approval at 10:15:01, since Q2 keeps a link open until every request sent on it has had its answer
options.says: Q2 stops each component in turn; without a drain in the manager's stop nothing waits for requests in flight

options.text: the approval at 10:15:01, since QMUX keeps the answer and hands it to the caller when the client is back
options.says: an answer that arrives on a closed connection never reaches QMUX; the caller's request ends with null

origin.section: 15.4 Drain a Link Before You Sign It Off

concepts: Each failure the echo limit allows keeps a dead host in the pool for one more echo timeout, and every purchase sent there is an unknown outcome to reverse.
A host sign-off that no listener takes ends on the unhandled queue; the link stays enabled and every purchase on it is declined until the logon mark expires.
